correctness.rationale: Positive 2x2 block matrices and the polar decomposition imply U*PU+Q >= 2a. A nonzero intersection of the low spectral projection of P+Q with its polar-unitary conjugate would violate this quadratic-form bound. Center-valued modular dimension then gives the half bound; a conjugated pair of inequalities yields the polar-Hermitian threshold improvement.

originality.rationale: Qualified to the best of our knowledge. The 2026 matrix sources prove eigenvalue versions but do not state the polar-wandering projection relation or center-valued finite-von-Neumann consequence. Related tau-measurable positive-block literature was checked as the main prior-art risk; no matching statement was located.

value.rationale: The result converts a sharp matrix median inequality into a projection-packing mechanism valid in arbitrary von Neumann algebras and a center-valued comparison theorem in finite ones, including type II algebras. It also unifies the general and polar-Hermitian thresholds and records sharpness and the failure of the one-sided-modulus analogue.
